title: Chicago artists call for action in rally against AI-generated music: ‘We don’t need it’
key_facts: More than 20 Chicago artists rallied against AI-generated music, tech companies and streaming platforms such as Spotify, on Thursday (1 Oct 2026, from the article's 2 Oct date).
They demanded legal safeguards against AI-generated copies of their work and labels that tell real music from fake music.
They plan a 'music platform blackout' on 26 and 27 October, asking listeners to avoid streaming platforms such as Spotify and Apple Music.
Many argued that AI music is built on existing music scraped from the web, which they see as stealing from decades of recorded work.
Musicians booed a 2025 remark by the leader of AI music platform Suno that most people do not enjoy the time they spend making music.
The article says streaming platforms have been slow to combat AI fakes of real artists and have sometimes welcomed AI-generated music.
Participants hinted the rally could start a longer campaign, perhaps based in Chicago; the rally lasted about half an hour.
quote_evidence: “We want policy that says: ‘This is fake music, and this is real music,’” said Melody Angel, a Bronzeville-based musician.
During that blackout, planned for Oct. 26 and 27, the group wants listeners to avoid using streaming platforms such as Spotify and Apple Music.
Streaming platforms have been slow to combat AI fakes of real artists and have sometimes welcomed AI-generated music.
why_it_matters_hint: A small but organised group of working musicians is asking for legal labels on AI music and a listener boycott, showing creative workers' anger over AI tools trained on their work.
event_date: Thursday 1 Oct 2026 (inferred from 'Thursday's rain' in an article dated 2 Oct 2026)
notes: Single outlet; claims about AI music 'stealing' are the participants' views. The date of the rally (1 Oct) is inferred from the article's date and its mention of Thursday. The article reports no response from streaming platforms or lawmakers.
